statement: Cboe Global Markets, Inc.'s Options segment revenues less cost of revenues increased 15% for the three months ended March 31, 2025 compared to the same period in 2024.
The Options segment's operating income increased $41.1 million for the three months ended March 31, 2025 compared to the same period in 2024.
The Options segment's operating expenses increased $3.9 million for the three months ended March 31, 2025 compared to the same period in 2024.
Assurant, Inc.'s Global Housing Adjusted EBITDA decreased $72.7 million, or 44%, to $92.4 million for Third Quarter 2024 from $165.1 million for Third Quarter 2023.
The decrease in Global Housing Adjusted EBITDA was primarily due to $110.6 million of higher pre-tax reportable catastrophes.
Excluding reportable catastrophes, Global Housing Adjusted EBITDA increased $37.9 million, or 20%, primarily from continued top-line growth within Homeowners.
Motorola Solutions, Inc.'s Products and Systems Integration segment revenue increased 13% in FY2024 Q3 compared to the same period in the prior year.
The 13% increase in the Products and Systems Integration segment included $3 million from unfavorable currency rates.
Expedia Group's lodging segment accounted for 82% of total worldwide revenue in the third quarter of 2024.
Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated's net product revenues increased to $2.8 billion in FY2024 Q3 compared to $2.5 billion in FY2023 Q3.

The increase in net product revenues was primarily due to increased TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO product revenues from strong global demand, including in younger age groups, and higher net realized pricing in the U.S.
NextEra Energy, Inc.'s NEET VIE owns and operates an approximately 280-mile electric transmission line.
The NEET VIE's assets and liabilities totaled approximately $679 million and $336 million, respectively, at June 30, 2024.
NextEra Energy Resources consolidates a VIE with a 10% direct ownership interest in wind and solar generation facilities capable of producing approximately 400 MW and 599 MW, respectively.

American Tower Corporation's property portfolio included 29 operating data center facilities across ten markets in the United States as of December 31, 2024, comprising approximately 3.3 million NRSF of data center space.

The data center facilities are located in specific markets including San Francisco Bay, CA (9 facilities, 998k NRSF), Los Angeles, CA (3 facilities, 724k NRSF), and Northern Virginia, VA (5 facilities, 651k NRSF).
IQVIA Holdings Inc. is a leading global provider of clinical research services, commercial insights, and healthcare intelligence to the life sciences and healthcare industries.
Oracle Corporation's cloud and license business represented 83% of total revenues on a trailing 4-quarter basis.
Cloud services and license support revenues now constitute 74% of Oracle's revenue and are growing by $1 billion this quarter.
Visa Direct processed nearly 10 billion transactions in fiscal 2024 for more than 550 partners.
Visa Direct utilizes more than 75 domestic payment schemes, more than 15 real-time payments schemes, more than 15 card-based networks, and more than five payment gateways.
Visa Direct has the potential to reach more than 11 billion endpoints through 4.0 billion cards, 3.5 billion bank accounts, and 3.5 billion digital wallets.
Viatris Inc. performed an interim goodwill impairment test for its five reporting units as of March 31, 2025, due to a decline in share price and increased geopolitical and economic uncertainty.
BorgWarner Inc. provided services to PHINIA at a cost of $3 million during the three months ended June 30, 2024.
PHINIA provided services to BorgWarner Inc. at a cost of $1 million during the three months ended June 30, 2024.
Mohawk Industries' results in Brazil benefited from strength in exports throughout South America, pricing actions, and enhanced mix.
Wynn Resorts, Limited excludes pre-opening expenses, property charges, corporate expenses, and stock-based compensation from EBITDAR calculations for its gaming operations.
Bristol Myers Squibb Co. reported a $19 million reduction in provisions for product sales for the three months ended June 30, 2024, compared to $11 million for the same period in 2023.
Bristol Myers Squibb Co. reported a $61 million reduction in provisions for product sales for the six months ended June 30, 2024, compared to $98 million for the same period in 2023.

Nasdaq, Inc.'s Index Revenues increased in the second quarter and first six months of 2024 compared with the same periods in 2023 primarily due to higher AUM in exchange traded products linked to Nasdaq indices and growth in trading volume on futures contracts linked to the Nasdaq-100 Index.
The increase in Index Revenues for the first six months of 2024 includes a $16 million one-time item related to a legal settlement to recoup revenue.
NRG Energy, Inc. completed $320 million of open market share repurchases during the three months ended March 31, 2025, at an average price of $99.52 per share.
As of April 30, 2025, $1.2 billion remained under NRG Energy, Inc.'s $3.7 billion share repurchase authorization.
NIKE Direct revenues grew 6% from $5.4 billion for the second quarter of fiscal 2023 to $5.7 billion for the second quarter of fiscal 2024.
NIKE Direct represented approximately 45% of total NIKE Brand revenues for the second quarter of fiscal 2024.
Deere & Company markets agricultural equipment through approximately 1,600 independent dealer locations in the U.S. and Canada.
Deere & Company sells turf equipment at most John Deere agricultural equipment locations and additional locations in the U.S. and Canada.

Deere & Company sells construction, earthmoving, material handling, roadbuilding, compact construction, and/or forestry equipment through approximately 450 independent dealer locations in the U.S. and Canada.
APA Corp completed the acquisition of Callon Petroleum Company in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $4.5 billion on April 1, 2024.
The Callon acquisition includes approximately 120,000 net acres in the Delaware Basin and 25,000 net acres in the Midland Basin.
Lockheed Martin’s MFC business segment recognized a reach forward loss of approximately $100 million in the first quarter of 2024 due to the probable exercise of an option on a classified contract.
The cumulative losses recognized on the MFC classified program reached approximately $150 million by the end of the first quarter of 2024, including prior period precontract costs.
Applied Materials, Inc.'s Semiconductor Systems sales are to customers in the foundry, logic and other; DRAM; flash memory markets.
The foundry, logic, and other market includes both leading-edge and non-leading edge technology nodes.
The non-leading edge technology nodes serve markets such as internet of things, communications, automotive, power and sensors.
3M Company's Solventum ownership change resulted in a $1.6 billion year-on-year benefit in 2024 following Solventum's separation in April 2024.
Tyson Foods, Inc. reported an increase in cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash of $575 million for FY2025 Q1 compared to the same period in the prior year.
The increase in cash and cash equivalents and restricted cash was partially offset by cash used for financing activities of $195 million and a $28 million decrease due to exchange rate changes.

Automatic Data Processing, Inc.'s Employer Services revenues increased due to new business started from New Business Bookings, strong client retention, an increase in pricing, an increase in interest earned on funds held for clients, and a favorable impact of one percentage point from foreign currency.

Employer Services' margin increased for the three and six months ended December 31, 2023 due to contributions from client funds interest revenues and operating efficiencies for costs of servicing clients on growing revenue, partially offset by increased investments and costs to develop, support, and maintain products, and increased selling expenses.
Employer Services' pays per control growth remained at 2% for the second quarter.
Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc.'s Global ARPU increased 1% for the three months ended September 30, 2024, and 3% for the nine months ended September 30, 2024.

The increase in Global ARPU was primarily attributable to subscriber growth of the ad-lite tier domestically, higher pricing, and a continuing subscriber mix shift from linear wholesale, partially offset by growth in lower ARPU international markets.
PACCAR Inc. plans capital investments in the range of $700 million to $800 million and R&D expenses in the range of $460 million to $500 million for 2025.
CME Group Inc. declared a regular quarterly dividend of $1.25 per share on February 6, 2025, payable on March 26, 2025, to shareholders of record on March 7, 2025.
The first quarter 2025 dividend payment is expected to total approximately $455.0 million, assuming no changes in the number of shares outstanding.
International Business Machines Corporation's Infrastructure segment profit decreased 13.8 percent in the third quarter of 2024 compared to the prior-year period.

The decrease in Infrastructure segment profit and margin was due to revenue decline from product cycle dynamics in IBM Z and Distributed Infrastructure, along with continued investments in innovation for next-generation products.
Infrastructure segment profit of $1,387 million decreased 9.3 percent in the first nine months of 2024 compared to the prior-year period.
Insulet Corporation's International Omnipod revenue increased $113.3 million, or 27.6%, in 2024 to $523.4 million compared with $410.1 million in 2023.

The 27.6% increase in International Omnipod revenue was primarily due to higher volumes from the launches of Omnipod 5 in the United Kingdom and Germany in 2023, driven by a growing customer base and conversions to Omnipod 5, along with a higher average selling price for Omnipod 5 compared to previous models.

Excluding a 0.7% favorable impact from currency exchange, the remaining 26.9% increase in International Omnipod revenue was primarily attributed to higher volumes from Omnipod 5 launches in the UK and Germany in 2023.

Realty Income Corporation granted 285,242 performance shares to executive officers during the three months ended March 31, 2025, with vesting tied to Total Shareholder Return performance and operating metrics over a three-year period.

The performance shares are recognized on a tranche-by-tranche basis over the service period, with 50% vesting upon achievement of goals during the performance period and the remaining 50% on January 1 of the following year, subject to continued service.
As of March 31, 2025, the remaining share-based compensation expense related to the performance shares totaled $34.2 million.
Northrop Grumman Corporation's first quarter 2025 product costs decreased $60 million, or 1 percent, compared to the prior period.
Chubb Limited's P&C net premiums earned increased 3.3 percent in FY2025 Q1 compared to FY2024 Q1, comprising growth in commercial lines of 4.2 percent and consumer lines of 7.1 percent.
Nasdaq, Inc.'s Capital Markets Technology revenues increased in 2024 compared with 2023.
The increase in Capital Markets Technology revenues was primarily due to the inclusion of revenues from Calypso associated with the acquisition of Adenza.

Capital Markets Technology revenues were also driven by higher trade management services revenues, mainly from demand for additional colocation and connectivity services following a data center expansion.
BIOGEN INC. expects drug pricing and other health care costs to continue to be subject to intense political and societal pressures on a global basis.
BIOGEN INC. faces risks of reduced revenue due to government price controls in certain countries, which may limit revenue and affect market growth.
BIOGEN INC. may experience adverse impacts on sales or reimbursements from government agencies due to budgetary or political constraints.
Bristol Myers Squibb's U.S. revenues decreased 7% during the first quarter of 2025.
The decrease in U.S. revenues was offset by increased demand across the Growth Portfolio and Eliquis, partially offset by generic competition impacting Revlimid, Sprycel, and Abraxane.
International revenues decreased 3% during the first quarter of 2025, primarily due to foreign exchange impacts.

Arch Capital Group Ltd. acquired RMIC Companies, Inc. and its subsidiaries on June 3, 2024, representing a run-off mortgage insurance business with $3.6 billion in insurance in force at June 30, 2024.
The acquisition increased Arch Capital Group Ltd.'s U.S. primary mortgage insurance in force by 1.2% at the end of FY2024 Q2.
Visa Inc.'s service revenue increased primarily due to 9% growth in nominal payments volume over the three and six-month prior-year comparable periods.

Visa Inc.'s data processing revenue increased primarily due to 11% and 10% growth in processed transactions over the three and six-month prior-year comparable periods, respectively, and select pricing modifications.

Visa Inc.'s international transaction revenue increased primarily due to growth in nominal cross-border volumes of 16% and 17% over the three and six-month prior-year comparable periods, respectively, excluding transactions within Europe, partially offset by lower volatility of a broad range of currencies.
Visa Inc.'s other revenue increased primarily due to growth in consulting and marketing services and select pricing modifications over the three and six-month prior-year comparable periods.
Visa Inc.'s client incentives increased primarily due to growth in payments volume over the three and six-month prior-year comparable periods.

Sysco Corporation is evaluating the potential impact of the OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework on Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (Pillar Two) on future periods, with the rules expected to be effective for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2024, and specifically for Sysco in fiscal 2025.
Lam Research Corporation's memory market segment revenue decreased from 48% to 44% of total revenue between December 24, 2023, and March 31, 2024.
The decrease in the memory market segment was partially offset by increases in the Foundry market segment, driven by spending from Lam Research's domestic China customers in the March 2024 quarter.
Domino's Pizza, Inc.'s U.S. franchise same store sales increased 5.2% in the two fiscal quarters of 2024 compared with the two fiscal quarters of 2023.
U.S. franchise advertising revenues increased $13.5 million, or 12.1%, in the second quarter of 2024.
U.S. franchise advertising revenues increased $11.1 million, or 4.9%, in the two fiscal quarters of 2024.
American Water Works Company, Inc. (through Cal Am) has incurred $266 million in aggregate costs related to the Water Supply Project as of September 30, 2024, including $84 million in AFUDC.
The Water Supply Project cost estimates approved in 2016 total $279 million plus AFUDC at a rate representative of Cal Am’s actual financing costs.

Teledyne Technologies Incorporated reported a 1.5% year-over-year increase in sales of electronic test and measurement systems, which include oscilloscopes, protocol analyzers and ethernet traffic generators.
Huntington Ingalls Industries, Inc. had 1,260 Master Shipbuilders at Newport News and 213 at Ingalls as of December 31, 2024.
The company employs over 44,000 employees, including approximately 7,000 engineers and designers and 4,600 employees with advanced degrees.
The acquisition mentioned in the remarks increased the workforce by approximately 500 highly trained personnel.

Quanta Services, Inc.'s Renewable Energy segment experienced increased demand due to the transition to a reduced-carbon economy, driving demand for renewable generation and related infrastructure such as high-voltage electric transmission and substation infrastructure, as well as interconnection services.

The Renewable Energy segment's increased demand was partially offset by supply chain challenges in 2022 and 2023, which caused project delays and increased material costs, particularly for solar panels in the utility-scale solar industry.
Nucor Corporation's current ratio was 2.5 at the end of the first quarter of 2025 and at year-end 2024.
Cash used in investing activities by Nucor Corporation increased by $290 million in the first quarter of 2025 compared to the first quarter of 2024, reaching $1.18 billion.
Capital expenditures for Nucor Corporation in the first quarter of 2025 were $859 million, an increase of $189 million from the prior year period.
Nucor Corporation's capital expenditures for 2025 are estimated to be approximately $3.00 billion, compared to $3.17 billion in 2024.
The primary capital expenditure projects for Nucor Corporation in 2025 include the sheet mill under construction in West Virginia and the construction of two manufacturing locations to expand NTS.
Equity Residential's Expansion Markets experienced elevated competitive new supply, requiring wider use of Leasing Concessions to attract and retain residents.
Moody's Corporation's Decision Solutions (DS) segment global revenue grew 11% in the three months ended March 31, 2025 compared to the same period in 2024.
The 11% growth in DS global revenue was driven by increases in the U.S. (21%) and internationally (5%).
The growth in DS segment was partially attributed to strong demand for MA's KYC solutions and acquisitions, including CAPE Analytics and Numerated.
ARR (2) growth for the DS segment was 12% in the three months ended March 31, 2025.

Arthur J. Gallagher & Co. may face material adverse effects on its financial condition and results of operations if a default under its debt financing obligations remains uncured or if necessary waivers from lenders are not obtained.

The company's reinsurance securities business involves using capital and short-term borrowings to purchase securities from reinsurance company clients, which exposes it to counterparty risk from investors.
Credit rating downgrades could increase Arthur J. Gallagher & Co.'s financing costs and limit access to financing sources, particularly if the company needs to raise capital in the future.
A credit rating below investment-grade could lead to increased operational risks, including higher operating costs and greater competitive pressures for Arthur J. Gallagher & Co.
The company's ability to meet debt obligations depends on dividends and other payments from its operating subsidiaries, as it is a holding company with no significant operations of its own.
